seoDescription: Learn how Vue.js organizes a project created with the Vue CLI: explore the src folder, assets, main.js bootstrap, and the root .vue component. Understand how Webpack and Babel enable ES6 imports, how the root component is rendered into index.html, the .vue file structure (template, script exporting component object, data as a function, methods, and scoped styles), and practical editing to create your first view file.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Vue CLI project structure**
  - The **src** folder contains the application code you'll edit.
  - The **assets** folder is for images and static assets.

- **main.js bootstrapping**
  - Imports **Vue** and the root **App.vue**.
  - Creates a new **Vue instance** and uses a **render** function to mount the root component into the element with the app ID in **index.html**.
  - ES6 imports are enabled by **Webpack** and **Babel**.

- **.vue single-file component anatomy**
  - **<template>**: component HTML; must have a single root element.
  - **<script>**: export the component object (name, data, methods, etc.).
  - **data** must be a **function** for components; ES6 shorthand (data() { return {...} }) is accepted.
  - **methods** hold component functions that can be invoked from the template.
  - **<style>** controls component CSS.

> [!TIP] Name your root component and keep the template simple while you get familiar with mounting and rendering.

> [!NOTE] The render(h => h(App)) pattern is the standard bootstrapping approach when using single-file components with the Vue CLI.

> [!IMPORTANT] Templates must have a single root element; otherwise the component will fail to compile.

## Practical Takeaways

- Open and inspect **main.js**, **App.vue**, and **index.html** to understand how they connect.
- Create a simple title in data and a greeting method to verify your component renders correctly in the browser.
- Familiarize yourself with the single-file component structure before adding nested components in later tutorials.
